autoscaler: a program that adds and removes copies of a server as load changes
replica: one running copy of the server
replica-seconds: the cost of keeping one replica running for one second
median: the middle value, with half of the measurements below it
p50: the median latency, so half of requests finish faster than this
p99: the latency that 99 out of 100 requests beat
latency: the time from sending a request to receiving its answer
throughput: how much text the server writes per second, summed over all requests
token: a short piece of text, often a word or part of one, which the model writes one at a time
concurrency: how many requests are being served at the same moment
in flight: accepted by the server and not yet answered
continuous batching: serving many users' requests through one copy of the model at once
KV cache: per-conversation scratch space the model keeps on the GPU while generating
engine: the program that loads the model and answers requests
vLLM: the open-source engine used here to serve the model
max-num-seqs: the engine's setting for how many requests it runs at once
out of memory: the GPU had no memory left for what it was asked to hold
service curve: latency and throughput of one replica, measured at each level of concurrency
cold start: the wait while a machine boots and loads a model, before anyone gets an answer
cooldown: a pause after the autoscaler acts, during which it does not act again
dead time: the delay between asking for capacity and that capacity being able to serve
backlog: requests that have arrived and are still waiting for service
queue depth: how many requests are waiting for a turn, per replica
utilisation: the share of each half-second sample in which the GPU was running any work at all
nvidia-smi: NVIDIA's command-line tool for reading GPU statistics
Little's Law: the rule that the average number of requests in a system equals their arrival rate times the average time each stays
RunPod: the GPU rental service these experiments ran on
worker: one RunPod machine running one copy of the server
load balancer: the front door that spreads incoming requests across workers
scaler value: an endpoint setting that RunPod documents as an autoscaling setting
open loop: requests sent on a fixed schedule, whatever the server is doing
closed loop: a fixed number of requests kept outstanding, with a new one sent as each finishes
pre-registered: written down and committed before the data existed
simulator: a program that imitates the system on made-up traffic instead of running the real thing
policy: one complete choice of the settings an autoscaler runs with
threshold: the signal value at which an autoscaler acts
frontier: the policies that no other policy beats on both axes
dominated: another policy is at least as good on both axes and better on one
Monte Carlo: answering a question by running many random trials and counting what happens
residual: the real value minus the predicted value
host: the physical machine a worker runs on
bin: a ten-second slice of the test, judged on its own
